name: Victorian
origin: Victorian print brought together many revival styles, ornate advertising, and expanding production methods. Treat the period as a family of approaches, rather than a single mandatory palette.
build: Draw a decorative border as SVG; keep its ornament separate from the text.
Combine a restrained reading face with one ornate heading treatment. Use a scanned or painted paper texture sparingly.
exercise: Frame one event announcement with original ornament. Remove half the decoration and compare what remains legible.

name: Art Nouveau
origin: Art Nouveau linked applied art, illustration, architecture, and lettering through flowing natural forms. On a website, its curves can guide attention around a clear content structure.
build: Draw flowing paths and botanical ornaments in Inkscape. Export reusable SVG frames.
Place readable HTML text inside the frame; preserve generous room around elaborate letterforms.
exercise: Draw one stem that branches into three section dividers. Reuse the same line weight and curve rhythm.
examples: Art Nouveau origins and visual examples

name: Art Deco
origin: Art Deco connects decorative craft with geometric modernity. Its stepped silhouettes and organized symmetry offer a different kind of richness from botanical ornament.
traits: Fine borders with contrasting display type
build: Construct a small library of stepped corners, fans, and repeated lines as SVG.
Use a clear central grid and carefully spaced display lettering; test all fine rules at mobile sizes.
exercise: Make a title frame from rectangles and straight lines only. Compare a centered and an asymmetric arrangement.

name: Bauhaus
origin: The Bauhaus brought art, craft, and industrial production into a shared educational project. Its legacy is broader than red circles and yellow triangles: structure and making matter.
traits: Type and image aligned to a deliberate structure
build: Build an asymmetric CSS grid with a small set of geometric SVG shapes.
Use size and position to establish hierarchy before adding color. Make every decorative shape earn its place.
exercise: Arrange one heading, one paragraph, and three shapes. Make a second composition with identical content and a different balance.

name: Swiss International
origin: Swiss International typography developed a systematic approach to visual communication. Grid relationships, photographic material, and clear information hierarchy are more useful lessons than copying one typeface.
build: Define columns, gutters, and a type scale in CSS. Align captions and images to the same underlying edges.
Use a few weights and inspect line breaks. Let empty space separate groups before adding borders.
exercise: Set a concert poster in two columns using only type, one photograph, and one accent. Explain every alignment.

name: Pop Art
origin: Pop Art brought mass-media imagery and everyday commercial culture into art. Digital interpretations often borrow repetition and graphic punch, but those visual effects are only part of its context.
traits: Halftone dots and flat color areas
build: Make a halftone pattern as a tiled SVG and crop an original photograph into repeated panels.
Keep functional labels clear when lettering becomes oversized or highly expressive.
exercise: Repeat one original object image four times. Change only its palette and observe how its mood shifts.
examples: Pop Art context and visual vocabulary

name: Memphis / Postmodern
origin: Memphis challenged restrained modernist taste with playful patterns, unusual combinations, and emphatic forms. A web adaptation can keep that energy while giving information a stable structure.
build: Create two repeatable SVG patterns and a small shape vocabulary.
Place them around a conventional content layout. Use pattern density to support, rather than obscure, hierarchy.
exercise: Design a section with one pattern, two shapes, and three colors. Test whether the main action is still immediately obvious.

name: Gothic
origin: Gothic architecture and lettering have long histories; a modern dark Gothic interface is a later interpretation. Pointed forms, vertical emphasis, and ornamental lettering do not require an unreadable page.
build: Draw pointed frames as SVG and prepare a restrained stone or paper texture.
Reserve elaborate lettering for short headings, with a clear reading face for descriptions and controls.
exercise: Make an original pointed-arch frame for a project title. Test its silhouette in one color before texturing it.

name: Editorial
origin: Editorial design organizes stories, images, and supporting information. Web editorial layouts adapt publishing practices to fluid screens, links, and changing amounts of content.
build: Use CSS grid for the story structure and set a comfortable paragraph measure.
Create reusable title, body, caption, and pull-quote roles. Keep the mobile reading order logical.
exercise: Lay out a project case study with a title, a lead paragraph, two images, and captions. Explain the reading order.

name: Minimal
era: Early 2000s web movement; earlier art roots
origin: Web minimalism reduces competing elements to focus attention on essential content and tasks. It is a decision process; an almost-empty screen is not automatically useful.
build: Start with content and remove elements that do not serve a task.
Use spacing and type hierarchy before containers. Check that links and controls remain recognizable.
exercise: Remove three elements from a project page. Explain whether each removal improves the task or simply makes the page emptier.
examples: Google in 1998: a comparison, not a movement date

name: Playful
origin: Playful describes an intended tone rather than one historical movement. Rounded forms, irregular illustration, and unexpected color can support it, but their use should fit the subject and audience.
build: Create one original illustrated motif and repeat its line and corner treatment.
Use motion only for specific feedback. Keep forms, labels, and reading order predictable.
exercise: Give one ordinary form a playful heading and illustration without changing the field labels or their order.

name: Dramatic / Cinematic
origin: Cinematic sites use composition and timed reveals to establish atmosphere. Film-promotion sites made this especially visible during the Flash era. The drama comes from coordinated assets and pacing.
build: Prepare separate image, title, and foreground layers. Animate a short sequence with CSS or a JavaScript timeline.
Use user-controlled audio and compressed video only where they add meaning. Provide a reduced-motion presentation.
exercise: Storyboard an entrance in three still frames before writing animation code.

name: Luxury
origin: Luxury communicates a desired perception, not a single historic style. Photography, production quality, restraint, or ornament may all contribute. Black and gold alone do not establish it.
build: Choose a material and photographic direction before choosing decorative effects.
Use exact alignment, consistent type roles, and a small accent system. Test fine borders and light type for contrast.
exercise: Design the same project introduction using light and dark backgrounds. Keep the imagery and hierarchy equally deliberate.
examples: Luxury as a contemporary visual direction

name: Nordic Minimal
origin: Nordic-inspired digital design borrows ideas of practical simplicity and material warmth. It is a broad interpretation of several design traditions, not a uniform Scandinavian rulebook.
build: Use clear typography, a modest spacing scale, and original or licensed material photography.
Avoid filling every surface with decoration; let content and useful controls establish the structure.
exercise: Build a reading panel with one photograph and no decorative container. Compare warm and cool neutrals.

name: Collage
origin: Collage combines separate visual fragments into a new composition. On the web it can mix photography, scans, illustration, and lettering while keeping links and text independent.
build: Mask original or licensed source images in an editor. Export fragments with transparency.
Position fragments in a responsive composition; keep essential copy as HTML and preserve a simple reading order.
exercise: Combine three original photographs and one paper texture. Keep a consistent light direction or deliberately explain its absence.

name: Cottagecore
origin: Cottagecore draws on idealized rural life and handmade domestic imagery. Its contemporary online expression references older craft and pastoral traditions rather than reproducing one period.
build: Draw original botanical dividers and photograph natural materials.
Use a small repeating texture beneath a clear reading surface, and test patterned areas behind text.
exercise: Create one botanical divider and repeat it across a page without turning every section into an illustrated frame.

name: Early web
origin: Early websites were shaped by available browsers, network speeds, and HTML capabilities. Their plain documents, image links, and dense directories span many looks rather than one universal style.
build: Use semantic HTML first, then deliberate borders and simple tiled graphics.
Keep the historical appearance while retaining keyboard access, responsive widths, and readable modern text sizes.
exercise: Make a small directory page that works without JavaScript. Give every link a meaningful label.

name: Terminal
origin: Terminal-inspired sites borrow text-based computing conventions. A green-on-dark screen is one reference, not the only historical terminal appearance. Clarity and useful feedback matter more than imitation.
build: Use real text, semantic links, and a system monospace stack.
Make any command interface optional and discoverable. Avoid fake error messages or motion that obstructs reading.
exercise: Present your projects as a readable text directory. Make every destination accessible without typing a command.

name: Pixel design
origin: Pixel-based graphic styles turn the image grid into a visible part of the design. Small icons and tightly controlled details were common in parts of the early web, alongside many non-pixel styles.
traits: Details aligned to an image grid
build: Draw at a small native resolution and preview at the intended display size.
Scale by whole-number factors when preserving hard pixels. Keep paragraph text separate from decorative bitmap lettering.
exercise: Draw one 24-by-24 icon with a four-color palette. Test it at its native size and twice that size.

name: Y2K
origin: Y2K design reflects overlapping visions of a digital future around the millennium. Some sites used metallic surfaces and technical type; others were colorful, playful, and translucent.
build: Build precise shapes as SVG and create metallic treatments through gradients or painted assets.
Export decorative graphics independently from labels and links. Low resolution alone does not create the aesthetic.
exercise: Create a capsule navigation button using three lighting bands, then make its normal and pressed states.

name: Grunge
origin: Grunge web graphics use roughness and distressed surfaces as expressive material. The look connects to wider print and music cultures; its web examples include many different levels of density.
build: Create masks from original paper scans, marks, or painted textures.
Keep a stable content layout beneath the rough surface. Test texture behind small labels and links.
exercise: Make one heading treatment from an original paper scan. Compare clean and distressed versions at phone size.

name: Flash-era worlds
origin: Flash was a multimedia platform, not a visual style. Its stage, timeline, and scripting encouraged coordinated animation, unusual navigation, sound, and scene-based websites.
traits: Scenes instead of ordinary page changes
build: Storyboard an interaction and prepare separate background, object, label, and effect layers.
Rebuild behavior using HTML, SVG, Canvas, or WebGL as needed. Sequence sound after user interaction and include reduced-motion alternatives.
exercise: Storyboard a menu entrance, a selection, and a transition. Describe which objects move in each frame.

name: Skeuomorphism
origin: Skeuomorphic interfaces reference familiar objects or materials to communicate use. A leather-bound notebook or physical-looking switch is more specific than a button that merely has a shadow.
build: Draw or render the material, frame, and control states separately.
Keep controls as real HTML elements over the artwork. Use consistent lighting and make the pressed state physically plausible.
exercise: Design an original wooden control panel with one blue button. Show its normal, focused, and pressed states.

name: Frutiger Aero
origin: Frutiger Aero is a later name for a cluster of optimistic, glossy digital imagery associated with this period. It overlaps with some Y2K traits but often emphasizes natural imagery and clean technological surfaces.
build: Combine an original landscape image with clear glossy controls and restrained highlights.
Layer a translucent surface above the image, keeping essential text on sufficiently solid backgrounds.
exercise: Make a glossy button on both a plain ground and a sky image. Compare whether the label remains readable.
examples: Y2K / Aero: a combined teaching interpretation

name: Synthwave
origin: Synthwave looks back at imagined electronic futures, borrowing from 1980s media and later music culture. It is a revival aesthetic, not a faithful copy of what every 1980s interface looked like.
build: Draw a perspective grid in SVG and use a small number of glow layers.
Create the horizon and lettering as separate assets. Keep functional text bright and free of heavy blur.
exercise: Create a horizon graphic with a grid and one light source. Make a readable navigation treatment beside it.

name: Vaporwave
origin: Vaporwave remixes consumer imagery, digital nostalgia, and music culture. Pastel palettes and classical fragments are familiar cues, but the broader aesthetic is about juxtaposition and reinterpretation.
build: Combine your own still-life or licensed imagery with geometric digital backdrops.
Use layered images and controlled gradients. Keep decorative lettering distinct from essential interface labels.
exercise: Build a small still life from three original fragments. Change the context with color rather than adding more objects.

name: Flat design
origin: Flat interfaces minimize simulated material and depth. Their simplicity can clarify structure, but overly subtle controls can make interactive elements harder to recognize.
traits: Hierarchy through scale, position, and contrast
build: Use CSS and simple SVG shapes for most surfaces.
Retain visible button boundaries, link styling, focus indicators, and clear hover or pressed feedback.
exercise: Remove decorative depth from one control while preserving all the clues that make it identifiable as a control.

name: Material-inspired
origin: Material is a maintained design system, not merely a shadow recipe. The Workshop preset is an interpretation; the official system includes components, interaction rules, and multiple generations.
build: Define surface, elevation, color, and type roles before individual components.
Use component states consistently. Study the official guidance rather than assuming every rounded card is Material.
exercise: Create a button, field, and panel with consistent focused, disabled, and active states.

name: Web Brutalism
origin: Digital brutalism often foregrounds raw structure and utilitarian presentation. It can reference architectural ideas, but it is not a direct translation of concrete buildings into CSS.
build: Start with semantic HTML and intentionally simple CSS.
Retain reading order and meaningful links. Distinguish purposeful restraint from a broken or inaccessible interface.
exercise: Present a project directory with no images or decorative containers. Make the link hierarchy unmistakable.

name: Neobrutalism
origin: Neobrutalism combines assertive graphics with more organized interface conventions. Its bold color blocks and hard shadows differ from the stripped-back appearance often associated with web brutalism.
build: Use consistent border and shadow tokens in CSS.
Reserve space for shadows and focus rings so they do not collide with neighboring content. Test the layout at enlarged text sizes.
exercise: Build one button with a solid offset shadow. Make pressing it feel like a small physical movement.

name: Neumorphism
origin: Neumorphism makes controls seem molded from the same surface as their background. The soft appearance is recognizable, but weak boundaries can obscure which elements are interactive.
build: Use paired CSS shadows on a simple surface and build a distinct pressed state.
Add clear labels, boundaries, and focus treatment; do not rely on subtle shading alone to signal action.
exercise: Compare a softly embossed button with a clearly outlined one in dim light and at reduced screen brightness.

name: Glassmorphism
origin: Glassmorphism uses translucent, blurred surfaces to imply depth. Earlier interfaces used related effects; the modern label describes a treatment that can coexist with many layout styles.
build: Use backdrop-filter with a sufficiently opaque background and a solid fallback.
Test text over every part of the underlying image. Keep menus and reading panels opaque when transparency hurts clarity.
exercise: Place one panel over two different backgrounds. Increase its opacity until both versions remain easy to read.
